summary: The submitted solution is largely incomplete: it returns a hardcoded default answer and does not implement the Two Sum logic. As a result it only passes 2/10 tests and fails on common cases (pair at end, negatives) and specified edge behavior (empty input). The main improvement is to implement the standard single-pass hash map approach and align behavior with the expected outputs for edge cases.

test_results.summary_note: Only 2/10 tests passed; failures show the function returns a fixed [0,1] instead of computing indices, and does not match expected empty-input behavior.

dimensions.what_to_improve: Implement the actual Two Sum logic (find indices i,j where nums[i]+nums[j]=target) instead of returning a hardcoded value; add handling to return [] when the input is empty to match the test expectation.

dimensions.name: Independence
dimensions.label: needs work
dimensions.what_to_improve: Even without hints, the submission didn’t make substantive progress toward a working algorithm; practice finishing a complete baseline solution (even brute force) before optimizing so you always have a correct, non-hardcoded implementation.

thinking_and_logic: The final submission does not contain an implemented algorithm: it iterates with a placeholder `pass` and always returns `[0, 1]`. This matches the answer-key’s known pitfall of hardcoding a visible example and fails on cases where the solution indices differ, and it does not conform to the expected behavior for an empty input per the provided tests.
code_assessment: Compared to the answer key’s optimal solution (single pass with a hash map of seen value -> index and checking the complement before inserting), the submitted code is missing the core technique entirely and therefore cannot achieve correctness or the intended O(n) performance. The canonical approach ensures you never use the same element twice and reliably returns the correct pair anywhere in the array; your current implementation always returns the same indices regardless of input, which directly caused the observed failures.

next_steps.action: Implement the canonical single-pass hash map solution for Two Sum.
next_steps.why: It is the expected optimal approach (O(n) time, O(n) space) and directly addresses the current correctness failures.
next_steps.how: Initialize `seen = {}`; for each index i and value x: compute `c = target - x`; if `c in seen` return `[seen[c], i]`; else set `seen[x] = i`; decide a fallback return (e.g., `[]`) consistent with the harness expectations.

next_steps.action: Add a small suite of self-check tests before submission.
next_steps.why: Your current failure mode is returning a hardcoded value; a few targeted tests catch that immediately.
next_steps.how: Manually run cases: pair at end, negatives, two elements (ensure ordering matches expected), and empty input if the platform includes it; verify indices are different and sum correctly.
